## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Āneñjakathā* (Kv 22.3) is a debate located in the twenty-second chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, the fifth book of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The controversy concerns whether an arahant or a Buddha passes away while in an immovable or imperturbable trance (*āneñja*) [Nyanatiloka 2007]. According to the commentarial tradition recorded by Nyanatiloka, this view was maintained by certain Uttarāpathakas [Nyanatiloka 2007]. The Theravāda position rejects the thesis on canonical grounds, citing the account in the *Mahāparinibbāna Sutta* (DN 16), which specifies that the Buddha passed away immediately after rising from—rather than while absorbed in—the fourth *jhāna* [SuttaCentral; Nyanatiloka 2007].
SuttaCentral lists one translation in one language and cross-references the sutta's citation of the *Mahāparinibbāna Sutta* (DN 16) [SuttaCentral].
